text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Bank of France cuts intervention rate to 3.15 from 3.20 percent, showing confidence in the franc's stability. Governor Jean-Claude Trichet calls for renewed investment from businesses and households, vows to carry on monetary stability policy. Targets for 1997 include a limit of five percent on growth in M3 money supply, compatible with limit in rise in prices of two percent, and GDP growth of about 2.5 percent GDP. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
LES ECHOS
-- A committee of members from Senate and National Assembly rule out reducing wealth tax.

-- Lagardere's Matra unit chairman Noel Forgeard in an interview says he opposes a public share float for Thomson-CSF on grounds that it would risk dismantling and weakening the defence firm. He draws from the recent U.S. McDonnell-Douglas and Boeing merger to call for the French defence industry to restructure around an aircraft industry hub, and an electronics hub, adds a future Thomson-Matra unit would create a European defence electronics leader.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls for banking sector reform, wants to alter a 1937 decree to increase working hour flexibility, reform status of savings banks Caisses d'Epargne.
-- Fifty-two firms were introduced on the Paris bourse in 1996, the best score since 1987.
LA TRIBUNE
-- New chairman of shipping business Compagnie Generale Maritime, recently bought by Compagnie Maritime d'Affretement, to restructure fleet over the next five years, merge the two firms' operations.
L'AGEFI
-- Association of Corporate Treasurers see 1997 GDP growth of 1.8 percent after 1.3 percent in 1996.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- New bank for small and medium businesses BDPME to start operations in January.
-- Former Aerospatiale chairman Henri Martre calls for creation of large European aeronautics group to fend off U.S. competition.
-- Sodexho catering group posts a 41 percent rise in profit for 1995-96, from last year.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Two new members of the Bank of France Monetary Policy Council to be chosen by December 29, markets to watch closely as reshuffle may alter monetary policy consensus.

-- Framatome nuclear plants manufacturer prepare for merger with GEC-Alsthom as parliament agrees to merger project, and Germany's Siemens sees alliance as not threatening its own co-operation with Framatome.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Statistics office INSEE sees peak in joblessness in 1997 at 13 percent over the first half, before a pickup in the economy brings the rate down.
